correctness.rationale: A self-contained executable reconstructs the 742 original faces, 30 invariant faces, 24,530 equivariantly subdivided faces, 12,414 quotient cells with orientation signs and d²=0, 6,100 genuine topological collapses and 104 integer-unit chain contractions. The residual integer boundary is (2,2,0,0), giving H2=Z/2 and H3=Z3. Separate finite-field ranks corroborate torsion and 73 group-presentation eliminations prove upstairs simple connectivity; Armstrong and simply connected 3-CW attaching classification yield the asserted Moore wedge. All quantified claims are about this complete finite complex; external mathematical theorem applicability is explicitly checked.

evidence: The Oct 25 full RESULT computes the complete integral B_4-module on unquotiented third homology, with a primitive diagonal relation among eight octahedral classes; it does not compute geometric orbit-space integral homology.
The Nov 8 full RESULT computes the rational B_4-character and predicts three antipodal-invariant third-homology rational classes; it does not compute the nonfree quotient integral cellular chains.
The new result computes degree-two torsion and three-dimensional attaching homotopy data.

evidence: Previous complete rational character implies invariant rational H_3 has dimension 3; this part is not novel.

The Rips complex has pairwise Hamming-distance at most 2 and excludes antipodal pairs, hence its antipodal geometric action is free and its fundamental group is Z/2. The present independence complex contains antipodal edges and has nonempty fixed point set, so its quotient fundamental group is trivial.
Complete integral direct quotient computation gives H_2=Z/2, and its three-dimensional simply connected CW model determines the Moore wedge decomposition.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The known rational rank is only one proper consequence. Neither that rank, the original integral lattice, nor the Rips-quotient result implies the new 2-primary Moore summand or homotopy type. Standard Armstrong and three-dimensional CW arguments complete the claim only after the new finite fixed-locus and integer-chain calculations.

evidence: Q_4 is graph-isomorphic to C_4 square C_4, the fully periodic four-by-four grid (not the open board). Bousquet-Melou et al. arxiv:math/0701890 treat square-grid independence complexes, focusing their homotopy results on open and cylindrical cases.

Conant--Thistlethwaite arxiv:0808.0739 §§2,6 explicitly define theta as Alexander dual to independence and study theta of hypergraph quotients, not a geometric quotient of the independence realization.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The antipodal involution on Q_4 corresponds to half-period translation in each of two C_4 factors. The geometric quotient is not the independence complex of the graph quotient, nor the Alexander dual of the theta complex of a quotient hypergraph, and its integral homology is not determined by replacing vertices by orbit labels.

value.rationale: Bit complement is a canonical central symmetry of the four-cube, and its fixed locus makes the quotient a motivated nonfree integral topology problem distinct from known rational and integral upstairs representation calculations. The exact H2 two-torsion and full Moore-space wedge resolves meaningful missing orbit-space information and is not merely a known Betti rank, an arbitrary graph slice or a routine change of notation. Higher cubes are expressly left open.
